name: Post-Marxism
summary: Post-Marxism, as Laclau and Mouffe set it out, keeps Marxism's emancipatory aim while giving up economic determinism, the privileged revolutionary role of the working class, the Jacobin idea of revolution and the hope of a reconciled, transparent society. Its positive project is a radical and plural democracy reached through a hegemonic articulation of many struggles (class, feminist, anti-racist, ecological) inside liberal-democratic institutions. Politics is held to be inherently conflictual, with opponents treated as adversaries, and Mouffe's later work adds agonistic pluralism, a multipolar world, left populism against neoliberalism and a left-wing protectionist, reformed Europe. The authors present it as a strategy, not a policy programme.
scope: The Laclau-Mouffe strand that the defining sources identify: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy (1985; 2nd ed. 2001), their 1987 reply 'Post-Marxism without apologies', and Mouffe's later agonistic and left-populist books (Agonistics 2013 and her 2016 left-populism interview), which the scholarship (Sim; Moreira) treats as the development of the same project. It excludes autonomist and Negri/Hardt currents, the Budapest School and ex-Marxists who became liberals. Mouffe's later books concentrate on political strategy, so most economic and social-policy statements are left unanswered.

sources.author: Cambridge University Press, Reflections on Postmarxism
sources.usedFor: Rejection of the working class as inherently revolutionary, support for new movements, and Mouffe's pluralism against universal norms.

sources.title: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy: Towards a Radical Democratic Politics, 2nd edition (Verso, 2001), third-party copy hosted by Platypus
sources.author: Ernesto Laclau and Chantal Mouffe
sources.usedFor: Rejection of class centrality, economism, vanguardism and Jacobin revolution; radical and plural democracy; the 2001 preface on neoliberalism and the redistribution/recognition question.

sources.author: Chantal Mouffe
sources.usedFor: Agonistic pluralism, rejection of consensus, multipolar world, critique of a coercive UN and of Westernizing democratization, free trade and the EU.

sources.author: Pedro Gois Moreira
sources.usedFor: Scholarly account of Laclau as a founder of post-Marxism and of the pluralist, anti-essentialist radical project.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: A footnote of Hegemony and Socialist Strategy (chapter 1) calls the assertion that capitalism will mechanically collapse 'so absurd' that nobody has upheld it, and denies the inevitability of socialism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy rejects the 'ontological centrality of the working class' and the classism of the Left, and treats class as one position among many antagonisms.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 2) treats 'rule by the people', that is popular sovereignty, as one of the two constitutive principles of the liberal democracy it defends.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Mouffe's 2016 interview says democracy means 'not only the rule of the majority, but also respect for minorities', which political liberalism brings.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy counts the gay movement and struggles against sexual discrimination among the democratic struggles to be articulated in a left hegemonic project.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Agonistics (introduction) rejects the universalism that postulates 'the rational and moral superiority of Western modernity' and urges a pluralism of cultures and forms of life.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Agonistics (the chapter on the post-democratic condition) calls the present 'post-democratic' condition one in which the value of equality has been set aside, so procedures alone do not make a democracy.

democracy-needs-political-clash.rationale: Agonistics and Mouffe's 2016 interview make irreducible conflict between adversaries the core of democratic politics and treat consensus politics as its danger.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Laclau and Mouffe's 1987 reply names 'new forms of domination established in the name of the dictatorship of the proletariat' among the reasons socialism must be rethought.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 2) rejects Bobbio's coercive world 'Third Party Judge' for the UN, saying such a democratic international Leviathan 'can only be a global hegemon'.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: The 2001 preface to Hegemony and Socialist Strategy locates the value of liberal democracy in 'the principles of liberty and equality for all' and aims to extend them to more social relations.

free-trade.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 3) says the 'ideology of free trade' must be debunked and that the reality of its effects is 'exactly the opposite' of its supposed benefits.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy (chapter 3) studies 'the institutions and practices through which the category of woman is produced' and treats sexual differences as constructed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 2) says liberal democracy is contextual, 'does not represent a more advanced stage', and that democracy can take other forms in other contexts.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy calls for a chain of equivalence linking struggles against sexism, racism, sexual discrimination and for the environment with those of workers.

local-production.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 3) criticises production oriented to export instead of domestic demand and calls for economic development on a regional perspective.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The 2001 preface to Hegemony and Socialist Strategy rejects the 'no alternative' neoliberal orthodoxy and calls for a project that 'restores the centrality of politics over the tyranny of market forces', with different modes of regulating markets.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy (chapter 1) is a sustained critique of economism and the base/superstructure scheme, holding that political articulation, not the economy, shapes social identities and outcomes.

material-over-identity.rationale: The 2001 preface says the solution is not to abandon the 'cultural' struggle and return to 'real' politics, and insists the Left must tackle both redistribution and recognition.

multipolar-world.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 2) advocates 'the establishment of a multipolar world' of regional poles organised on different models, in place of a unipolar order.

national-mission.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 2) rejects imposing the Western democratic model worldwide as a source of new antagonisms.

night-watchman-state.rationale: In her 2016 interview Mouffe says that under neoliberal hegemony the left is 'constrained to defend' the welfare state it once wanted to radicalize, so she does not limit government to protection from violence.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy (chapter 3) approves the critique of feminist essentialism that rejects a preconstituted category 'women's oppression' with a single mechanism, while warning against one-sided dispersion.

one-party-rule.rationale: Agonistics makes legitimate adversaries who compete within shared institutions the core of democratic politics, which excludes a party with an exclusive right to lead.

parliamentary-road-socialism.rationale: Mouffe's 2016 interview describes a 'radical reformism' that engages in institutions as Syriza and Podemos do, and Hegemony and Socialist Strategy says radical democracy has a socialist dimension ending capitalist relations of production.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy calls for extending democratic rights beyond the traditional field of citizenship, including true participation by all subjects in decisions on production, with forms adapted to each social space.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy (chapter 3) says every construction of sexual difference 'invariably constructs the feminine as a pole subordinated to the masculine', so one can speak of a sex/gender system.

political-decisions-consensus.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 1) rejects the aim of 'a consensus, without exclusion' and says antagonism 'reveals the very limit of any rational consensus'.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 1) says opponents must be adversaries, not enemies, and blames confrontations 'over non-negotiable moral values' for violence.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 3) calls the crisis one of the EU's neoliberal incarnation, not of the European project, and wants a socio-political project to win citizens' allegiance to the Union

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 2) says the claim that democratization means implementing the Western liberal democratic model worldwide must be relinquished, since enforced universalization provokes violent reactions.

public-ownership.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy (final chapter) says radical democracy implies a socialist dimension and names the socialization of the means of production as one element of its strategy, though not mere workers' self-management.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy (chapter 3) denies that humanist values rest on an essence and studies how 'Man' is produced historically; Agonistics reformulates human rights pluralistically.

single-common-good.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 1) criticises Rawls and Habermas for aiming at a rational consensus on the 'common good' and says conflict and exclusion cannot be removed from politics.

smash-state-machine.rationale: In her 2016 interview Mouffe calls left populism a 'radical reformism' that engages with institutions and transforms them in a radicalizing and pluralizing sense; Agonistics (the chapter on the post-democratic condition) wants to re-establish democratic values without relinquishing liberal representative institutions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy rejects the working class as the privileged agent of socialism and says socialism is one component of radical democracy, not the reverse.

state-harmful.rationale: In her 2016 interview Mouffe says left populism is 'not opposed to democracy and institutions' but transforms them, which excludes abolishing the state.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 1) says democratic politics treats opponents 'not as enemies to be destroyed, but as adversaries' whose ideas are fought but whose right to defend them is not questioned.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Agonistics (ch. 3) defends 'a left-wing form of European protectionism' to build an ecological and social industrial base and cites South American governments protecting domestic industries.

total-state.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy criticises 'statism' and holds that the multiplication of political spaces and the autonomy of spheres of struggle is incompatible with concentrating power in one point.

vanguard-party.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy (chapter 2) calls the Leninist vanguard conception 'ever more vanguardist and anti-democratic', with a manipulative relation between vanguard and masses.

workers-councils.rationale: Agonistics (the chapter on the post-democratic condition) wants democratic values restored without relinquishing liberal representative institutions, and Hegemony and Socialist Strategy treats workers' self-management as insufficient, so class councils do not replace parliaments.

workers-own-party.rationale: Hegemony and Socialist Strategy says a whole conception of socialism resting on the ontological centrality of the working class is in crisis, and proposes alliances of many struggles instead.

missingStatements.text: Political and social identities are constructed through discourse and political struggle, not fixed by a person's economic position.
missingStatements.rationale: Laclau and Mouffe criticise essentialised class identity and treat the identity of social subjects as discursively formed.

missingStatements.text: Politics is inherently conflictual, and rival groups should be treated as adversaries within democratic institutions rather than enemies to be eradicated.
missingStatements.rationale: Mouffe says conflict cannot be eliminated, only channelled, with opponents recognising each other as adversaries.

missingStatements.text: The working class is not the privileged agent of social change; many different struggles must be linked together.
missingStatements.rationale: They reject the idea that the working class is inherently revolutionary and defend women's, anti-racist and ecological movements alongside it.

notes: Themes searched in the saved texts: class and history, revolution and violence, state and institutions, vanguard and party, democracy, pluralism and consensus, welfare and markets, trade and protection, Europe and the UN, multipolarity, democratization abroad, ecology and growth, feminism, race, sexuality, unions, immigration, nationalism, religion, property, technology and the rest of the statement list. Most economic, social-policy and national-question statements are null because the texts concentrate on political strategy and do not take them up. This pass replaced answers resting on Wikipedia pages and one interview with answers from the primary texts; every changed answer keeps its earlier version in reviewHistory. Sources s3 and s4 (Wikipedia) remain listed only because earlier versions in reviewHistory cite them. The NLR citation rests on the article's opening paragraphs, which are on the free page.

keyFigures.role: Co-author of Hegemony and Socialist Strategy, which coined the term post-Marxism
keyFigures.quote: the name of Ernesto Laclau, one of the founders of post-Marxism, was highlighted as an influence
